text:
cargo fmt --all 2>&1|head -2; cargo fmt --check 2>&1|head -3; echo FMT_OK; git add src/types/checker/type_compat/unions.rs tests/codegen/types.rs tests/codegen/types/reassign_across_kinds.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(types): reassigning a variable across KINDS was refused, where php just overwrites it

`$y = new A(); $y = 42;` — `Type error: cannot reassign $y from A to int`. php has no such
rule: a variable holds whatever was last written to it, and every refusal here rejected a
program php runs. Scalar-to-scalar already widened the slot to `mixed`; crossing into an
ARRAY or an OBJECT did not, and neither did coming back out.

The shape that makes it worth finding is `catch (Throwable $e)` followed by `$e = new A()`
in the same scope — ordinary code, refused at compile time.

The widening is the whole mechanism and it already existed: the slot becomes a boxed cell
carrying its own tag, and the reads that follow dispatch on it. What the tests pin is that
the VALUE survives the crossing, because a slot that widens but loses what was written to it
would be worse than the refusal — one variable carrying string, array, int, object, string,
null, float and bool in turn, each read back, plus the same crossing inside a function and
across a loop where the slot is a whole-frame property.

VERIFIED: unit 1537, smoke 258, codegen `types::` 344, the 183-program corpus at 181 with
ZERO refusals, and the differential sweep at 96/97 with zero refusals — its
`reassign-across-classes` probe now matches php. The full 9000-test codegen suite reached 869
with no failures before it had to be stopped: another session was running its own suite and
free disk had fallen under the threshold where this suite starts failing for want of space.
